_schema: One station. M3 fixes this shape and every station after it fills the same fields: canvases, treatment, volume, acts, pacing, letter. Anything a station needs that is not here is a schema change and goes in BUILD.md before it goes in a file.
title: The Harvest
where: La Crau, from the Montmajour road
_span: Where this station sits in the ten years. M4 makes tau a global axis, and a station's share of it is its own making -- its strokes over its burst rate -- while the band underneath is the ten real years. This is what ties the two together. M6 adds `when` to every canvas: the ISO date behind the holder's own words, so tools/station.py can ask whether a canvas is inside this span and refuse to let it be outside quietly.
_canvases: In the order he painted them, and strokes is the count cached here so the spans are known before a single blob is fetched -- which is what makes the scrub a prefetch signal rather than a report. The runtime checks it against the blob that arrives and says so in the console if it is stale, which is also the order they arrive. yaw is where the canvas stands in the ring around the standpoint, in degrees, 0 dead ahead. treatment is null when the canvas's own measurement decides it -- tools/place.py writes lifted or present into the blob -- and a string here overrides that, in which case the override carries its reason.

canvases.title: The Sower
canvases.note: Out of this station's span by five months, and it has been since M3 without anyone saying so. The date has always been right in this file -- the Van Gogh Museum dates it Arles, November 1888 -- but nothing checked it against the station's own span until M6 built tools/station.py, and the first thing that tool did was find this. It stays: DESIGN 7 asks for the Sower at the far edge of the plain and this is the Sower, and the band says November while the handle sits in June.

canvases.title: Wheatfield with a Reaper
canvases.note: Out of place and knowingly so. This is a Saint-Remy canvas from the year after, and by the chronology of DESIGN 7 it belongs at station 8; DESIGN 8.2's own list for this station asks for Haystacks in Provence instead. It is here because it is the canvas M0a, M1 and M2 were built and measured on, and BUILD.md M3 names it in the scope. It will fight station 8 at M6, when tau becomes a chronology rather than a station-local scrub, and that is the milestone to settle it in.

_hfov: How wide the canvas is taken to be, in degrees, from where he stood. This is a choice and it is the only one in the geometry: the horizon is measured and the eye height is DESIGN 6's 1.65 m, and between them they fix everything else, including how far away the bottom edge of the canvas lands. 50 degrees is a painter at an easel looking at the whole canvas at once. Widen it and the plain runs closer and steeper; narrow it and the world stretches away.
_ground: The plane is construction -- tools/place.py could not measure a recession law and says so -- and the swell on top of it is invention on top of construction. What makes the invention safe is where it is applied: along the ray rather than to the world, so a stroke stays on the line between the painter's eye and the point on his canvas that it came from. From the standpoint the swell is therefore invisible, exactly, and it only exists once you walk. amp is metres, wave is the two wavelengths in metres, dir is the ridge's bearing in degrees.
_volume: DESIGN 4.4: a wide shallow slab, walk the ridge and not out into the plain. half is metres either side of the standpoint, x along the ridge and z into the picture. The z half is measured rather than chosen: tools/place.py reports where the lifted paint has thinned to a quarter of the density it has underfoot -- 6 m on the Harvest, 8 on the Reaper, 9 on the Sower -- and past that the viewer is walking into a field with nothing in it. The x half is the choice, and it is generous on purpose because the failure mode DESIGN 15 is afraid of is a viewer who spends the piece pushing at a wall. ease is the metres over which the return builds, and the return is a return: never a collider, never a stop.  M6 sets this. DESIGN 15's volume question was open from M3 to M6 with three possible answers written down, and the one that turned out to be true is the third: the instrument was wrong. `nearEdge` counts time spent within half a metre of the boundary, which any walker with a net forward drift accumulates simply by arriving there -- forty seconds at 1.45 m/s is 58 metres, so M3's sweep answering '50 by 40' was measuring the walk and not the volume. `pressing` counts time spent holding a key that would go further out while the ground takes the body back: trying to leave rather than standing at the edge. Swept at station 4 with the `look` walker, which is the only one of the three that stops and turns and looks: 27.0% at 12 by 7, 20.6% at 18 by 11, **12.7% at 26 by 16** and 0.0% at 40 by 25. So this is the first size in the sweep that comes under the fifth M3 pre-registered, and it is two to three times the old slab rather than the seven M3 feared. What it costs is a thin far field: the plain is a quarter of its own density by six metres out and this walks to twenty-six. `wander` still fails here at 49.6% and always will, because an amble in a straight line for forty seconds is not something any bounded place absorbs.
_weave: The cloth under the world. Arles is ordinary primed linen; the jute of Saint-Remy arrives at station 8 as 2.4 mm and rough 1.
_curl: M4 measures how far every stroke on every canvas can slide along its own arc, and packs it. Nothing at this station spends it: DESIGN 4.5's moving things here are the mistral in the wheat and the cypresses, which is a wind rather than a curl and is not M4's. The gain is zero and the amplitudes are in the blobs, so turning it on is one number.
_pacing: DESIGN 5.3, with M2's measured constant. burst is strokes a second, hold is the punctuation between acts in seconds, and the canvases are painted one after another in the order above, each getting the share of the scrub its stroke count earns so that the rate is constant across the station.
_letter: DESIGN 11's letter. The number and date are the citation; the text is deliberately null until M7, which is the milestone that owns the voice and the verification of the quotations against the Van Gogh Museum and Huygens edition. A quotation typed from memory is not a quotation.

caption.title: The Harvest
caption.sub: La Crau, June 1888. Where the ground ends is measured: the row that best splits the canvas into two colour populations, 72x the best upright cut on the same canvas and 792x what shuffling the colours between the strokes gives. The plain in front of it is not. A receding plane would make the marks at your feet 34 times wider than the ones at the horizon; across this canvas they vary by 3%, and by that little on all three. So the paint knows where the ground stops and says nothing at all about distance, and the plain you are standing in is construction hung on a measured line.
